  Context (read-only review; do NOT edit repo files, do NOT commit):
  - Repo: /Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern, branch formal/access_model_0.1. Lean project in formal/ (Lean 4.35, core only, no Mathlib). Build: cd formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake build. Scratch Lean files: write ONLY under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/review3/ (create it) and run with cd formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean <file>. Test contracts are available in the module: KT sh pinned done dealloc compat, K0, KA, KF; states are built with enterEff/enterEff S3.init ..., deriveEff, transferEff, exitEff, endUseEff, freeEff, issueEff, etc.; verdicts are checked with `.ok (by decide)` / `.reject (by decide)` (see the test-case section at the end of formal/Ern/MM03.lean for many examples).
  - Module under review: formal/Ern/MM03.lean (namespace Ern.MM03), pass 2 of milestone 1. Pass-1 version for comparison: git show f39ab7a:formal/Ern/MM03.lean.
  - Normative spec: /Users/guygouri/Downloads/ERN_Memory_Model_0.3.3.md (MM-03.3 v0.2). Task brief with binding arbitrages A1-A11 (they override the spec where they speak): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/task_mm03_p2.md.
  Rules (AGENTS.md): a definition says exactly what its rule says (not stronger, not weaker); no unjustified hypothesis; no theorem weakened or made vacuous; interpretation must be explicit; every finding needs evidence (spec/arbitrage quote, a Lean counterexample checked by decide, or command output). No evidence, no finding. No requests beyond the task.
  
  You are a skeptical judge. For EACH finding below, try to REFUTE it: re-run the Lean evidence, read module, spec and arbitrages. Confirm only if the evidence holds and the issue is real and within the task. Default to refuted if evidence does not hold.
  
  Findings (lens lean):
  [
   {
    "title": "issue on a full arena whose blocks are still live returns reject, not fail (A10); the 'full arena -> fail' test only passes because it was built artificially",
    "severity": "major",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:3099-3102 (IssuePre, region clause l.3101), 3132-3139 (IssueStep), test n10a l.3763-3768, test l.3579",
    "cause": "Formalization error, plus a test built artificially. IssuePre requires `effective s ar.internal l = some .modify` on the region. A live block derived from `internal` suspends that right, so every unavailable region whose block is still active fails the static precondition and yields `reject`. `fail` can only happen for a region that was issued and whose block was later ended, before any reset. A10: \"issue : ok | fail | reject, fail (état inchangé) si la région est indisponible\". The task's case \"issue sur arène pleine -> fail\" is satisfied only by first ending both blocks (n10a docstring: \"both regions issued, both blocks ended, no reset\"). MM-03.3 §11 forbids this: \"le rapport doit le signaler explicitement plutôt que construire artificiellement un exemple donnant le verdict attendu\".",
    "evidence": "Checked by `lake env lean` on /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/review3/cx.lean (CX1). The file has no errors; a control false example in the same file does error. Setup: a0 = enter1 [(none,none,0),(none,some 0,0),(some 1,some 0,0),(some 1,some 0,0),(none,none,0),(none,none,0),(none,none,0)], ar0 = ⟨1,1,[2,3],[]⟩. Issue [2]->4 then [3]->5 (both `.ok (by decide)`), giving a2. Then: `a2.2.available = []` and `¬ Avail a2.2 [2]`, both by decide. `IssueStep KA a2.2 0 [2] 6 a2.1 .reject := .reject (by decide)`. `¬ IssueStep KA a2.2 0 [2] 6 a2.1 (.fail a2.1 a2.2)` is proved. Every other IssuePre clause holds by decide (MetaRight, Active internal, Usable 6, HasRight .modify 6, no Init leaf in 6), and `effective a2.1 1 2 = none`. So the region is unavailable and the outcome is reject. The existing test at l.3579 (`IssueStep KA c6b.2 0 [2] 5 c6b.1 .reject`) shows the same behaviour.",
    "fix": "Report the conflict between A10 (fail when unavailable) and the static effective-Modify clause, which is reject. This is the clause A11 relies on for the disjointness redundancy. Ask which outcome wins when a region is unavailable because a live block holds it. Replace n10a with a full arena whose blocks are live, or have the report flag the case as not representable."
   },
   {
    "title": "A2 '≥' read as '≥ the mode of the held authority': one Observe sharing of a value makes its owned storage unreachable, even for reads by the owning frame",
    "severity": "major",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:602-607 (S3.Exercisable.held, l.607 `Allows (effective s b l) y.mode`), 610-616 (exR)",
    "cause": "A2 leaves out what the effective mode must be ≥ to: \"une autorité exerçable de mode effectif ≥ sur toute l'empreinte de p\". The code picks the mode of the held authority, so Exercisable does not depend on the mode being exercised. A root of owned storage is a Modify authority held by the owning place. As soon as the owning value has an active Observe descendant, nobody can exercise that root: no read and no derive. This interpretation changes accepted programs and is not flagged as an ambiguity (AGENTS: 'If the spec is ambiguous ... stop and report').",
    "evidence": "cx.lean CX2, all by decide. b0 = write3Eff (enter1 [(none,none,0),(none,some 0,0)]) [0,1]. `Read3Step 1 [1] b0 (.ok b0)` holds. After one observation, b1 = deriveEff b0 0 0 .observe (`DeriveStep ... (.ok b1)`), the following hold: `Read3Step 1 [1] b1 .reject`, `DeriveStep 1 1 .observe b1 .reject`, `¬ b1.Exercisable 1`, while `Read3Step 2 [0] b1 (.ok b1)` still holds. A callee given the Observe parameter (b2 = enterEff b1 [2] [(none,none,0)], EnterStep ok) can read the value (`Read3Step 2 [0] b2 (.ok b2)`) but not its owned storage: `Read3Step 1 [1] b2 .reject` and `DeriveStep 1 1 .observe b2 .reject`. Compare MM-03.3 §11 case 1, \"Deux observations d'une même feuille | Autorisé\".",
    "fix": "Report the A2 ambiguity: ≥ the held authority's mode, or ≥ the mode requested by the operation. Ask for an arbitration. The second reading would make Exercisable mode-indexed."
   },
   {
    "title": "Owned places of the ended or freed value: endUse blocks accesses to them, free does not; after free, a logically dead owned place is still readable and its root is released while a descendant is active",
    "severity": "major",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:2666-2667 (EndingLeaf), 2682-2685, 2704-2710 (EndUsePre), 2790-2796 (freeS), 2804-2807 (FreeAccessOK), 1016-1017 (canRead3)",
    "cause": "A6 does not say what happens to accesses on places owned by p, which die logically. endUse widens A6's \"aucune autorité active dérivée sur l'empreinte de p détenue ailleurs\" to the leaves of places that stop being usable (EndingLeaf), which is stronger than A6's literal text. The pin clause is widened the same way. free keeps A6's literal wording (leaves of p only). The two operations are therefore inconsistent. With free, a place owned by p becomes unusable while an access held by the frame stays active and readable, since canRead3 does not check usability. Its origin, the root held by p, is released anyway, although O3.2 would refuse that release. Neither choice is reported as a spec gap.",
    "evidence": "cx.lean CX3a/CX3b, by decide. (a) n6x = write3Eff (enter1 [(none,none,0),(none,some 0,0)]) [1]; e1 = deriveEff n6x 1 1 .observe (DeriveStep ok). `footprint e1.P 0 = [0] ∧ e1.afp 2 = [1]`, yet `EndUseStep K0 0 e1 .reject`: no derived authority covers the footprint of p=0. (b) f0 = enter1 [(none,none,0),(none,some 0,0),(none,some 1,0)]; f1 = write3Eff f0 [2] (ok); f2 = deriveEff f1 2 2 .observe (ok). With KF1 = KT [] [] [] [1] [(1,7)]: `FreeStep KF1 1 7 f2 (.ok (freeEff f2 1))`. Afterwards: `¬ (freeEff f2 1).Usable 2 ∧ (freeEff f2 1).freed 2 = false`, `(freeEff f2 1).Active 3 ∧ ¬ (freeEff f2 1).Active 2`, and `Read3Step 3 [2] (freeEff f2 1) (.ok _)`, a read of a dead place. In the same state f2, `EndUseStep KF1 0 f2 .reject` and `ReleaseStep 2 f2 .reject` both hold. free_no_dangling (l.2909) covers only `footprint s.P p`, so it does not catch this.",
    "fix": "Report the A6 gap (accesses and pins on places owned by the ended or freed value) and get an arbitration. Then apply the same rule to endUse and free."
   },
   {
    "title": "ArenaInv does not make `internal` the root of the storage: issued regions may lie outside the administered storage (weaker than A10, §6 and pass 1)",
    "severity": "major",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:3072-3081 (ArenaInv), 3099-3102 (IssuePre)",
    "cause": "Formalization error, and a pass-1 statement weakened. A10: \"stockage = emplacement possédé par la valeur arène ; internal = sa racine\". §6: \"Les régions émises sont incluses dans le stockage administré\". Pass 1 had `∀ l ∈ ar.storage, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal`, with issued and available regions ⊆ storage. Pass 2 only requires regions ⊆ `afp internal`, with `internal` any Modify root held by the storage's owner. Nothing links `afp internal` to `footprint s.P ar.storage`.",
    "evidence": "cx.lean CX5, checked. h0 = enter1 [(none,none,0),(none,some 0,0),(none,some 0,0),(none,none,0)]: place 1 is the storage and place 2 is another place owned by 0. arH = ⟨1, 2, [2], []⟩, where internal is authority 2, the root of place 2. `ArenaInv h0 arH` is proved. `IssueStep KA arH 0 [2] 3 h0 (.ok h1.1 h1.2)` holds by decide. Then `footprint h1.1.P arH.storage = [1] ∧ h1.2.issued = [([2], 4)]`, so the issued region is not in the storage.",
    "fix": "Add to ArenaInv that `s.afp ar.internal = footprint s.P ar.storage`, or that it covers it, and check the arena theorems still hold."
   },
   {
    "title": "§10 theorem release_restores_authority (and pass-1 split_unsound_without_DD) removed in pass 2 and never rebuilt",
    "severity": "major",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean (absent); pass 1: git show f39ab7a:formal/Ern/MM03.lean l.1514-1517 and l.2527-2529; removed in commit 2a56a2a",
    "cause": "Missing coverage. MM-03.3 §10 lists `release_restores_authority` among the milestone-1 theorems. Commit 2a56a2a says \"Pass-1 proofs and test cases are removed here and rebuilt in later steps\", but no later step restores it. The task also requires each removed or rewritten pass-1 statement to be justified. The pass-1 counterexample showing that the `DDSound` hypothesis is necessary (split_unsound_without_DD) is also gone, so nothing now shows that the hypothesis of split_preserves_underDD and reachable_access_invariant_underDD is needed.",
    "evidence": "`comm -23` of the theorem names in pass 1 (f39ab7a) against pass 2 lists release_restores_authority and split_unsound_without_DD, among others. `grep -n \"restor\" formal/Ern/MM03.lean` finds nothing. `git log -S release_restores_authority` shows it was last touched in 2a56a2a, the removal.",
    "fix": "Restate and prove release_restores_authority on the pass-2 state, or justify its removal. Restore the DDSound counterexample."
   },
   {
    "title": "free requires `OwnedRoot` (no parent), a condition A6 does not state, added to make WF3 preservation go through",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:2781-2782 (OwnedRoot), 2827 (FreePre), 2879-2888 (free_preserves uses hroot)",
    "cause": "Unjustified hypothesis. A6 asks for \"un emplacement possédé\" with \"K.Deallocable p (unité libérable selon le contrat de l'allocateur)\". Whether a unit can be freed is the contract's call. A part of an owned place is itself owned (WF3: a part has its parent's owner). Requiring `parent = none` adds a restriction, and it is exactly what free_preserves needs to keep WF3's dead-flag clause for parts.",
    "evidence": "cx.lean CX4, by decide. g0 = enter1 [(none,none,0),(none,some 0,0),(some 1,some 0,0),(some 1,some 0,0)] with KG = KT [] [] [] [2] [(2,7)]. `FreeStep KG 2 7 g0 .reject` holds and `¬ OwnedRoot g0 2`, while every other FreePre conjunct holds: Deallocable, FreeCompat, Usable 2, HasRight .modify 2, FreeAccessOK, FreeAnchorOK, pins. Also `(g0.P[2]?).map (·.owner) = some (.place 0)`, so place 2 is owned.",
    "fix": "Report the restriction as a spec question, or leave it to K.Deallocable and handle parts in WF3 and the effect."
   },
   {
    "title": "A7 re-anchoring stops at authorities held by places, while A7 says 'held by a surviving frame'; the interpretation is not flagged",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:952-970 (Survives, firstSurv, exitG), 976-983 (ExitPre)",
    "cause": "Spec defect, handled by an unflagged interpretation. A7 reads: \"Ré-ancrage itéré ... jusqu'à la première autorité active détenue par un cadre survivant ; reject si la chaîne atteint la racine d'un emplacement du cadre sortant\". Under A4 and A10, chains can end at a root held by a place, for instance `internal`. The literal A7 then gives no outcome: no frame-held authority is found, and the root is not one of the exiting frame. The code treats any live holder (a frame or a usable place) as surviving. Its docstrings justify this by A4/A5 without noting the gap in A7.",
    "evidence": "cx.lean CX6, by decide on test case 16: `(c16d.A[6]?).map (·.origin) = some (some 1) ∧ (c16d.A[1]?).map (·.holder) = some (.place 0)`. After the exit, the returned block keeps origin 1 (`internal`), which is held by place 0, not by a frame.",
    "fix": "Report the A7 wording gap and the chosen reading (surviving = HolderLive after the pop)."
   },
   {
    "title": "Docstrings claim more than the statements prove (exitFrame_kills_locals, free_marks_freed)",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:2433-2441 (exitFrame_kills_locals), 2929-2932 (free_marks_freed)",
    "cause": "Formalization error in documentation. The exitFrame_kills_locals docstring says a place owned by the exited frame is no longer usable \"nor is any place whose owner chain passed through such a place\". The statement covers only places with `pl.owner = .frame f`, so transitive possession (A5, task step 1) is not stated. The free_marks_freed docstring says \"`free` is the only operation that releases storage\". The statement only describes `freed` after free. Apart from endUse_no_dealloc_event, no theorem says other operations leave `freed` unchanged.",
    "evidence": "Statement at l.2440: `(∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f → ¬ s'.Usable q)`, with no clause for `.place` owners. Statement at l.2932: `∀ q, s'.freed q = (s.freed q || decide (q = p))`, under a FreeStep hypothesis only.",
    "fix": "Either state the transitive and exclusivity claims as theorems, or cut the docstrings to match the statements."
   }
  ]

## Claude Code

# AGENTS.md

Claude Code implements. Codex reviews. Both follow this file.

## Source of truth

- `specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics. Before acting, read the spec text the task depends on. Never rely on memory, summaries, comments or earlier sessions.
- Never restate spec content in code comments or agent files. Point to its location.
- Spec beats code. If the spec is ambiguous, contradictory or silent on something the task needs: stop and report the exact passage with a concrete example of the problem. Never pick an interpretation yourself.
- Representation choices (structure or inductive type, function or relation) are yours when they change no accepted program and no behavior. A choice that does is a semantic question: stop and report.

## Scope

- Do exactly the task. No unrequested features, generalization, refactoring or "robustness" additions. Put suggestions in the report.
- Do not edit `specs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `formal/DESIGN.md` unless the task says so.

## Lean

- The Lake project is in `formal/`. `formal/DESIGN.md` governs how to formalize, never what the semantics is. Propose design decisions it does not settle in your report; never take them silently.
- Every definition or theorem that encodes a spec rule cites the rule's location in its docstring.
- A definition says what its rule says. Never make a definition more permissive, add an unjustified hypothesis or narrow a theorem's domain to obtain a proof.
- Never change a theorem statement, or a definition it depends on, to make a proof go through. If stuck, stop and report the goal state.
- Never use `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `native_decide`.
- Every `.lean` file under `formal/` is part of the build target.
- Done means:
  - `lake build` (in `formal/`) succeeds;
  - this prints nothing: `grep -rnE '\b(sorry|admit|native_decide)\b|^\s*axiom\b' --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake .`
  - for each theorem completed by the task, `#print axioms` lists nothing beyond `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

## Report

Spec passages implemented (by location), what changed, what is unproven or open, spec problems found.

## Review (Codex)

Adversarial and read-only. For each change, check:

- It says exactly what the spec says: not stronger, not weaker. Read definitions, hypotheses and quantifiers, not only proofs. A theorem that holds because a definition is too permissive or its hypotheses are unsatisfiable is blocking.
- Each formalized rule cites its spec location.
- No theorem statement or dependency was changed without the task allowing it.
- No interpretation was chosen silently where the spec is unclear.
- Nothing outside the task was added.

When a milestone is declared complete, compare the rules in its announced scope with the spec locations cited in `formal/`, and list every rule left without a definition or theorem.

Every finding needs evidence: a spec quote, a counterexample or command output. No evidence, no finding. Never ask for additions beyond the task.

Output: verdict (block / changes / ok), then each finding with severity, location, cause (formalization error, missing coverage or spec defect) and evidence.
- [ERN formal exploratory passes](ern-formal-mm02-exploration.md) — French briefs, MM-02 branch, reports/ never merged, spec outside repo
